Compared with current scheduling algorithms supporting multiple priorities in a buffered crossbar, our project need not per priority queueing at per crosspoint, can not only avoid complicated scheduling in the fabric but also provide flow isolation and protection, and the implementation is relatively simple. Simulation results are presented to evaluate the delay property of our scheme, indicating that our scheme can match a buffered crossbar with per priority queueing at per crosspoint

articleTitle: Adaptive Modulation In MIMO System with AFE Constraints
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) configuration is a popular method for high data wireless transmission. In this paper an adaptive modulation scheme for MIMO channels was addressed. Assuming a block fading channel model and perfect knowledge of channel state, we invested adaptive modulation scheme that provides better throughput under the constraints on the power of each antenna analog front-end (AFE) which is the case of applications. Our analysis is based on the convex optimization. Then a low-complexity iterative bit-loading algorithm implementing this solution is also developed. The performance of the scheme is also examined through analysis and simulations

articleTitle: A Novel Low Distortion Switch Used in A/D Converter for Directly Sampling Bipolar Voltage Signals
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In order to directly and accurately sample a bipolar voltage signal into a unipolar supply A/D converter with normal CMOS technology, a novel low distortion switch is proposed. This novel switch is composed of only four PMOS transistors, one capacitor and one normal switch. It can directly sample a bipolar signal without a conventional used voltage level shift circuit and makes the circuit free of noise, distortion and temperature characteristics problems that are caused by voltage level shift circuit. This switch is one type of high linear bootstrapped switches, of which the source to gate voltage is kept to a constant value to reduce nonlinearity. A sample/hold circuit with this novel switch is implemented in a 12-bit SigmaDelta A/D converter with a standard 0.5 mum mixed mode CMOS process. By simulation, this sample/hold circuit achieves a 120 dB SFDR when sampling a 1 V peak-to-peak, 156 KHz bipolar signal under 10 MS/s sampling rate

articleTitle: Field Device Communication Based on IEEE 802.15.4
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: IEEE 802.15.4 is a useful standard for wireless factory communication. Based on it, we give several solutions for cyclic data and non-cyclic data transfer, among which GTS (guaranteed time slot) can be assigned while a device requiring dedicated bandwidth or low-latency. But the control process for GTS is so complicated that the performance is degraded in applications. In this paper, the problems caused by GTS management in cyclic data transfer are analyzed and a GTS pre-allocation in such situation is proposed. Then we give the optimized solutions for field device communication which have better performance of simple control, lower jitter, less latencies and the minimum modification to the standard

articleTitle: An Low Power Ultra-Wideband CMOS LNA for 3.1~8.2-GHz Wireless Receivers
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband (UWB) 3.1~8.2-GHz low-noise amplifier design. Resistive shunt-feedback method is used to provide wideband input matching and low noise figure (NF). The cascade configuration is employed with the inductive source degeneration and an input three-section band-pass Chebyshev filter. The LNA operates at 1.5 Volt and consumes 16.2 mW. At 3.1~8.2-GHz, this LNA has NF of 3.6 dB, with input return loss of -12.155 dB, output return loss of -12.75 dB, and power gain of 11.43 dB. The circuit is designed with TSMC 0.18 mum single-poly-six-metal CMOS process

articleTitle: Design of Collimation System in Space Laser Communication
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, semiconductor laser beam collimation lenses system which can be used in space laser communication has been optimum simulated and designed. Some new design methods based on the geometrical optical theory have been discussed in details, and an ideal aspheric surface design method has been given. The optical system has been further simulated by optical design software CODE-V. The collimation laser beam divergence angles have been obtained by experimental measure with laser beam analyzer. Experimental test results showed that it can be achieved a good collimation effect. This optimum design laser beam collimation system can be widely used in modern space laser communication

articleTitle: An Improved Estimation of Integer Frequency Offset in OFDM Systems Using ML Method
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we propose a simple maximum likelihood (ML) estimation method with one training symbol for the integral part of the carrier frequency offset between the transmitter and the receiver in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems. The carrier frequency offset is obtained by using the information of the training symbol. The performance of each estimator is compared through Monte Carlo simulation, and we show that proposed estimator performs better than the conventional one

articleTitle: An Overview on the Integrated IP Optical Data Control Plane in the Optical Transport Network
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In recent years, the optical transport network (OTN) systems have been introduced widely, however, wide adoption has been limited due to the immature infrastructural issues. The OTN infrastructure takes the responsibility of data and signal transmission for substratal layer, as well as provides carrying and maintaining services (mostly the IP-based traffic today) through an optical data transport control plane. Thus, this paper focuses on the latest OTN data control plane and therefore gives a comprehensive introduction on the integrated IP optical peer control plane

articleTitle: Precision Bits Can Be Reduced by One in Max-Log-MAP-Based Decoder
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The addition and taking the maximum (max) operations, as well as all the quantized data involved in the max-log-MAP turbo decoding algorithm form a commutative max-sum semiring. In this paper performance degradation of turbo decoding caused by shift operations using fixed-point data representation and unified precision bits is solved when the distributive law is properly applied to this semiring, with a bonus of considerable computational saving and precision bit reduction from 3 to 2 for all the pertinent variables with negligible performance degradation.

articleTitle: Multidimensional PR Filter Banks with FIR Filters
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Multidimensional perfect reconstruction quadrature mirror filter (QMF) banks with finite impulse response (FIR) filters induced from systems of biorthogonal multivariate scaling functions and wavelets are investigated. In particular, bivariate scaling functions and wavelets with dilation as an expansive integer matrix whose determinant is two in absolute value are considered. Demonstrative quincunxial examples are explicitly given

articleTitle: Turbo Decoder Early Detection Based on Density Evolution
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In maximum a posteriori probability (MAP) decoding of turbo code, the density evolution of decoder's internal variable alpha is shown to evolve to stability as the number of iteration increases. In this paper a new block-oriented early detection stopping criterion is derived from this property. Simulation results show that the bit error rate performance would drop almost negligibly if the criterion parameters are carefully chosen

articleTitle: An Efficient VLSI Architecture of Frequency Domain Kurtosis for Non-Stationary Acoustic Noise Measurements
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Recent research shows that the conventional energy-based metrics used for acoustic noise measurements underestimate the hazardous effects of non-stationary noises on hearing conservation practice. New strategies that adopt higher-order statistical metrics to quantify noise measurements are needed to better assess potential damage to hearing. This paper proposes an efficient architecture of the frequency domain kurtosis metric that is a higher-order statistical metric. The architecture emphasizes efficiency on area and time to meet the technological challenges of compactness and portability for the acoustic noise measurement instruments.

articleTitle: Scale, Rotation and Pose Invariant 3D Object Detection using Log-polar Transform and Singular Value Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper proposed a novel biologically motivated 3D object detection algorithm which works robustly in the presence of large scale changes, rotation, occlusion, and pose changes. The robustness to scale and rotation is achieved through log-polar transformation procedure. Singular value decomposition (SVD) in conjunction with the distance-to-feature space measure is used to handle the pose variations and reduce the computational complexity. The system was evaluated using 3D object with varying scale and pose on different complex backgrounds. The experimental results show that the object detector was quite robust to all these variations

articleTitle: Hysteresis-Current-Controlled Class-D Amplifier with Active Current Sensing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A hysteresis-current-controlled (HCC) class-D amplifier with active current sensing techniques is presented in this paper. The active current sensing techniques are used to sense and control inductor current. The class-D amplifier has been fabricated in 3.3-V, 0.35-mum double-poly quadruple-metal CMOS technology. The proposed class-D amplifier is suitable for current-mode and voltage-mode applications.

articleTitle: Delayed Fuzzy Controller Design for Hyperchaotic Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Studied in this paper is a new delay-dependent chaos control approach via delayed state feedback. This approach uses Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy model to represent original hyperchaotic system and adopts parallel distributed compensation (PDC) design technique. This method is universal one which works well for any continuous hyperchaotic system. As an illustrative example, its application is discussed in detail for hyperchaotic Chen's system

articleTitle: Content Protection for MPEG-4 Video with Watermarking
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a MPEG-4 video codec based watermarking scheme to protect video content. This scheme provides dual protection for intellectual property rights (IPR), utilizing error propagation in temporal MCP. Watermark is embedded into I-VOP, and is adjusted before I-VOP is reconstructed as reference VOP. During decoding, the embedded watermark in I-VOP is adjusted by the same way as in encoding. Only users with authorization can adjust the watermark correctly during decoding to get good video quality. For illegal users the video is also accessible but with bad quality because of the propagation of error caused by adjusted watermark in I-VOP. The watermark in I-VOP exists anytime once it's embedded. This scheme has the virtue of providing dual protection with little expense of time and computation. Some experimental results are given and discussed in the end

articleTitle: Neighbor Definition in P2P Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Neighborhood is a widely used and commonly understood concept in almost every network. Yet there is no formal clear definition of this concept for P2P networks. Here we present a conceptual and yet formal definition for neighborhood in P2P networks and will show that the definition will fit well in almost all its existing applications and definitions from other authors. The definition is mainly useful for unifying the various current definitions of neighborhood, classifying the protocols and comparing them.

articleTitle: 40-Gb/s 1:2 Demultiplexer in 0.35-μm SiGe BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A 1:2 demultiplexer was designed in 0.35-mum SiGe BiCMOS technology. An improved latch was used to realize the core cell of this circuit. Compared to the emitter-coupled-logic (ECL), the emitter-emitter-coupled-logic (E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>CL) used in this latch can increase its speed. The results show that this demultiplexer can operate at the data rate of 40-Gb/s. The whole circuit with single 5-V supply consumes 100 mA

articleTitle: Study on the Identification of Loading Materials for Initiating Explosive Device
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Neural network (NN) design is a key issue in the study of artificial neural networks. The use of genetic algorithm in searching the best hidden neurons makes the structural modular neural network less likely to be trapped in local minima than the traditional gradient-based search algorithms. Based on the analyses of the pressing model of loading materials for initiating explosive device and the cooperation of computing intelligent theories, an identification system of loading materials for initiating explosive device is developed on neural networks with genetic algorithms. Emphatically the experiment results show the identification requirement of loading materials for initiating explosive device can be satisfied in this system

articleTitle: Optimal Transport Format Detection for UMTS Uplink
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we describe a CRC-based optimal Blind Transport format determination algorithm with application in UMTS uplink. A MAP detector is derived. Simulation results under both AWGN and fading channel are given

articleTitle: Optimal Design on FIR Digital Filters Using the Parallel Algorithm of Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper introduces in detail the optimal design approach of high-order FIR digital filter and differentiator using the algorithm of neural networks. The main idea is to minimize the sum of the square errors between the amplitude response of the ideal FIR digital filter or digital differentiator and that of the designed by training the weight vector of neural networks, then obtaining the impulse response of FIR digital filter or differentiator. The convergence theorem of the neural-network algorithm is presented and proved, and the optimal design approach is introduced by examples of high-order FIR digital filter and digital differentiator. The results show that the high-order FIR digital filter or digital differentiator designed by training the weights of neural networks has a very high precision and very fast convergence speed, and initial weights are stochastic. Therefore, the presented optimum design method in the paper is significantly effective

articleTitle: Ideal N-type SiC/metal Contacts by Reduction of the Density of Interface State
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The ideal SiC/metal contacts were formed by controlling the barrier height on the ideal SiC surface. The ideal SiC surface was realized by lowering the density of surface states owing to SiC surface hydrogenation. The mechanism of surface hydrogenation was studied in this paper. Using the surface hydrogenation treatment, SiC Schottky diodes with ideality factor of 1.2-1.25 and ohmic contacts with specific contact resistance of 5 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>~ 7 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> Omega cm2 were obtained below 100degC for the first time. Its advantages lay in not only avoiding the annealing at 800-1200degC for Ohmic contacts in the conventional process, but also improving the electrical performances of SiC Schottky diodes.

articleTitle: Classifier Ensemble Selection for Language Verification System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Spoken-language verification system uses classifier combination method to improve its performance. The number of classifiers combined determines the system's costs in time and calculation. Hence, we aim to get the optimal classifier ensemble with less cost and good performance. We hope to find some characteristics of classifier ensemble closely linked to its equal error rate (EER) and then choose the optimal classifier ensemble based on them. Two new diversity measures were proposed. Through rank correlation coefficients between them and EER, we found new diversity measures had closer correlation with the performance of system. Final results showed combining two new measures is the most effective to choose the optimal classifier ensemble, which makes system 14.71% best relative decrease in EER and about 60% best relative decrease in costs. We also explored preliminarily the robustness of this method over open-set corpus.

articleTitle: A Downlink Grouping Transmission Scheme for TDD OFDM System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A downlink grouping transmission scheme has been proposed for TDD OFDM system. The coded bits are separated into several branches according to their priority, and then the results are adaptively allocated and transmitted on the 2-dimension time-frequency channel blocks, which are also separated into different groups according to their power. Simulation results show that this scheme can significantly improve the performance of TDD OFDM system. Meanwhile, the grouping modulation and downlink time-frequency channel prediction can further enhance the grouping transmission

articleTitle: A 3.8GHz Fully Integrated Digitally-Controlled LC Oscillator for PHS Transceiver
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel digitally-controlled LC oscillator (DCO) for PHS transceiver. This DCO is more suitable for system integration especially in a deep submicron CMOS process. The oscillator is designed in a 0.18 mum CMOS process with a central running frequency of 3.8 GHz and 630 MHz tuning range. The phase noise at 1.2 MHz offset frequency for 3.8 GHz is below -128 dBc/Hz while drawing 2.5 mA of current from a 1.8 V supply

articleTitle: Study for the Real-time Analysis Technologies of Broadband LargeDynamic Range Wireless Communication Signal
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper introduces the related technologies of analyzing for wireless communication signal with 10 MHz~8 GHz input frequency, 36 MHz real-time bandwidth, and at least 100 dB dynamic range. It especially describes such key technologies as system architecture based on RF (radio frequency) -IF (intermediate frequency) direct digitization, dynamic range extension and digital compensation based on both adaptive realtime AGC (automatic gain controlling) and channel delay synchronization, programmable re-configurable DDC (digital down converter) based on the integrated function of large scale FPGA (field programmable gate array) and DSP (digital signal processor), and the baseband analysis for multimode communication signal demodulation, etc. Provided with the simulation results, the technologies mentioned above can be testified their validity

articleTitle: The Analysis and Research for the Laser Beam through Random Atmosphere Channel
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In free space optical communication system, the characteristics of atmosphere affect laser transmission. These effects include absorption and dispersion of aerosol, dust, frog, rain, haze when laser beam through atmosphere. The laser power attenuation of the absorption and dispersion is introduced. Then the turbulence and its influence of flicker, bend and abruption are analyzed. At last the experiment research system and the test method are given. The experiments are carried out at the different air condition at the same time, in the different time at the same day and in the different visibility condition. The results are in accordance with theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Oblivious Routing Algorithm under Hose Model for WDM Mesh Network
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel oblivious routing scheme based on valiant load-balancing for the model of polyhedral uncertainty (i.e., hose model), and the scheme is implemented with traffic-grooming approach in WDM mesh networks. Considering that a high-speed connection request in optical networks is difficult to be divided into low-speed connections, we propose the method of hose-model separation to support the multi-granularity connections for valiant load-balanced oblivious routing in WDM mesh networks. Our Objective is to minimize total network cost. Two fast heuristic algorithms-MPCF and MRUF are proposed. Simulation results show MRUF performs better than MPCF

articleTitle: Keynote Speech Abstracts; 1. Nanoscience and Nanotechnology: Status, Potential and Roadmap
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In recent years, nanoscience and nanotechnology have attracted much attention and have posed much significant potential in many areas of societal interest. For instance, opportunities are presented for help solving global energy needs with environmentally clean solutions, increasing the quality of life through improved medicine and health care, improving the productivity of agriculture industry, and providing the benefits of information technology everywhere. Recent development of nanomaterials has enabled ever-clean cloths and nanobiosensor devices. NEMS in concert with nanoelectronics would help develop intelligent nanorobots for unique applications. In Feynman's words, "There is a plenty of room at the bottom." Although semiconductor industry calls its sub-100nm technology as nanotechnology, the room is much bigger than that of nanoelectronics. In this talk we will review the status along with potentials in various fields. Further we will discuss what can bring the realization of nanotechnology industry with some degree of acceleration in the world that becomes flatter and promotes international collaborations and competition.

articleTitle: Fast Blocking Artifacts Reduction Algorithm Based on Contrast Enhancement Technique
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A blocking artifacts reduction algorithm by enhancing image contrast in DCT domain is proposed. In order to save more computations, only two DCT coefficients are used to represent the edge information of the shifted block, and then construct an adaptive enhancement factor. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the traditional algorithms

articleTitle: A Backup LSP Bandwidth Reallocation Mechanism in MPLS Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a mechanism to make efficient use of the network resource by reallocating the backup LSP bandwidths to lower priority connections over separated links in network that support Differentiated Services-aware MPLS Traffic Engineering and 1:1 protection switching. Principles of the bandwidth reallocation mechanism and proposed bandwidth allocation algorithm are presented in this paper. Compared with a typical bandwidth allocation algorithm, the proposed algorithm can not only make more efficient use of the backup path resources, but also guarantee the QoS of the protection switching connection. Our algorithm has been implemented in the C programming language, and the experimental results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm

articleTitle: A New Method for Impossible Differential Cryptanalysis of 7-round Advanced Encryption Standard
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a new method for impossible differential cryptanalysis of 7-round advanced encryption standard. This attack on the reduced 7-round AES requires about 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">123.5</sup> chosen plaintexts, demands 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">89</sup> words of memory, and performs 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">122</sup> 7-round AES encryptions. Furthermore, it is only 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-34.5</sup> of the probability to fail to recover the secret key

articleTitle: New Frequency Divider with 8 Output Phases for Phase Switching Prescaler
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A 5.6 GHz divided-by-7/8 prescaler is presented. A phase switching technique is used, and the prescaler has 8 pi/4 -spaced output phases. Two parallel divided-by-2 flip- flops are usually used to generate 8 output phases, but this architecture suffers from the uncertainty of its output phase patterns. In this paper we propose a novel circuit which has four serially connected differential latches and which can generate 8 output phases without any phase-pattern uncertainty. It decreases the logic complexity of phase switching prescalers and improves the noise immunity which is an important merit when the PLL integrated with noisy digital circuits and in low-voltage implementation.

articleTitle: A Novel Algorithm for Constructing Light-Trees in Mesh WDM Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: It has been recognized that light-trees should be as balanced as possible in order to guarantee an adequate signal quality and to scale to large destination sets, if power losses are taken into account when routing connections in mesh WDM networks. In this paper we study the problem of constructing such balanced light-trees. We propose a novel algorithm, called extended shortest path heuristic algorithm (ESPH) and is an extended version of the well known shortest path heuristic (SPH) algorithm, for the problem. The ESPH algorithm aims to minimize the difference between the optimal signal quality and the worst signal quality in the process of constructing light-trees. Simulations on a typical mesh network are conducted to verify the performance of the ESPH algorithm. Results demonstrate that the light-trees constructed by the ESPH algorithm are more balanced than those constructed by the only existing algorithm, called BLT (balanced light-tree algorithm) for the same problem, with a little more cost. Thus light-trees constructed by the ESPH algorithm can provide better signal quality and are more scalable than these constructed by the BLT algorithm

articleTitle: Channel Capacity and Digital Modulation Schemes in Correlated Weibull Fading Channels with Nonidentical Statistics
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents the novel closed-form expressions for the average channel capacity of dual selection diversity, as well as the bit-error rate (BER) of several coherent and non-coherent digital modulation schemes in correlated Weibull fading channels with nonidentical statistics. The results are expressed in terms of Meijer's G-function, which can be numerically evaluated easily. The simulation results are presented to validate the proposed theoretical analysis and to examine the effects of the fading severity on the concerned quantities

articleTitle: Research on Hardware Built-in Computer Safety
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This article discusses the available concepts of hardware visualization techniques that enhance the computer system safety. Firstly it describes the existent methods such as execute disable bit (EDB) capability and virtual machine architecture (VMA) that are implemented in the general purpose processors. Then it introduces the execution disabling policies (EDP) method derived from the EDB capability. The EDP will provide an execution policing service that may be guaranteed by hardware for a function call. In this case every program will have a hardware verified certification to do a certain function. The article also introduces the concept of memory visualization based hardware cryptography being the enhancement to EDP and VMA

articleTitle: Keynote Speech Abstracts; 1. Nanoscience and Nanotechnology: Status, Potential and Roadmap
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In recent years, nanoscience and nanotechnology have attracted much attention and have posed much significant potential in many areas of societal interest. For instance, opportunities are presented for help solving global energy needs with environmentally clean solutions, increasing the quality of life through improved medicine and health care, improving the productivity of agriculture industry, and providing the benefits of information technology everywhere. Recent development of nanomaterials has enabled ever-clean cloths and nanobiosensor devices. NEMS in concert with nanoelectronics would help develop intelligent nanorobots for unique applications. In Feynman's words, "There is a plenty of room at the bottom." Although semiconductor industry calls its sub-100nm technology as nanotechnology, the room is much bigger than that of nanoelectronics. In this talk we will review the status along with potentials in various fields. Further we will discuss what can bring the realization of nanotechnology industry with some degree of acceleration in the world that becomes flatter and promotes international collaborations and competition.

articleTitle: The Application of Magnetoresistive Sensor in Detecting the Capsule's Localization in GI
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The paper reports the principle and characters of the magnetoresistive sensor and its application in the localization of the noninvasive monitoring capsule in GI (gastrointestinal tract). When the capsule's position is detected, the kind of sensor may be fixed inside the capsule, and the three coils for stimulating magnetic field are fixed outside body. Like this, the capsule's coordinate value can be calculated by magnetic theory. However, as a more excellent method, we can fix one cylindrical permanent magnet inside the capsule, and three magnetoresistive sensors are fixed outside the body. The capsule's coordinate values can be calculated by magnetic dipole theory, too. The relevant experiment indicates the novel method is simple and reliable. The method will probably be applied in practice with continually researching. Moreover, the magnetoresistive sensor will play important role in the localization system.

articleTitle: Low Complexity Motion Refinement for DCT-Domain Video Transcoder
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we address in the topic of spatial-downscaling video transcoder in DCT domain. The proposed techniques include the hierarchical fast motion resampling (HFMR) with accuracy motion resampling, and the fast refinement for non-integral-MV (FRNI) with low complexity motion vector refinement. For FRNI, it can be applied not only in our proposed algorithm but also combined with other video transcoders which have MC-DCT (motion compensation in DCT domain) and reduce overall the computational complexity. Furthermore, in combination of FRNI and HFMR, it will get the best performance compared with the conventional approaches. Experimental results show that our proposed algorithms can improve the entire quality and also reduce the complexity in MC-DCT

articleTitle: Optimization of Sparse Plane Arrays Using an Improved Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: For the element position synthesis of sparse rectangular plane arrays with the design constraints of the number of elements, the aperture and the minimum element spacing, an improved genetic algorithm (IGA) based on chromosome element resetting is presented in this paper. Compared with the synthesis method of thinned arrays, this new approach could exploit more degree of freedom of elements to control the characters of the sparse arrays. When the aperture, the number of elements and the minimum element spacing are fixed identical, the new approach can make the sparse plane array produce lower peak sidelobe level (PSLL). The simulated results show that the fitness function value of thinned plane arrays with 108 elements mentioned by Haupt can reduce 5.626dB when the minimum element spacing of half wavelength was introduced into the optimization. And as well, the great efficiency and the robustness of IGA are shown in this paper.

articleTitle: A New Calculation Method for Mutual Impedance Matrix and Its Application to DOA Estimation
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new calculation method for mutual impedance matrix is proposed. The mutual impedance matrix is derived from electromagnetic boundary conditions and can be used to relate the coupling free open-circuit voltages instead of the conventional one to the measured voltages. Its application to DOA estimation shows that the mutual impedance matrix obtained by our proposed method quantifies the mutual coupling effects more precisely than the conventional one

articleTitle: Scaling Behaviors of Traffic in Computer Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we present an empirical study on the scaling behaviors of traffic in computer communication networks. It is shown that the data shipped by the web server have a symmetry heavy-tailed distribution, with the corresponding cumulative distributions of both negative and positive tails can be well fitted by a Levy regime or an extendedly asymptotic power-law form. We investigate the long-range dependence of the absolute value of both packet-changes and byte-changes by using the detrended fluctuation analysis, and find a crossover at approximately 5 minutes (300sime10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sup> seconds) in both the two cases. The corresponding scaling exponents are 0.66/0.98 and 0.63/0.97 for the measure of packets and bytes, respectively

articleTitle: Simplification and Combination of Soft-in/Soft-out Iterative MMSE and MF V-BLAST Soft Interference Cancellation Detector
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Iterative soft-in/soft-out (SISO) minimum mean squared error (MMSE) soft interference cancellation (SIC) detector has been successfully applied to V-BLAST turbo receiver. To reduce the computation complexity, an iterative SISO SIC detector combined MMSE with match filter (MF) has been proposed. In this paper, we simplify the SISO MF SIC detector and propose two turbo receiver schemes, in which MMSE, MF and the simplified MF are combined to further reduce the computation complexity. Compared with the detection scheme with combination of MMSE and MF, computer simulation results confirm that the performance degradation of the proposed detector schemes is very trivial, but the computation complexity is reduced significantly

articleTitle: A New Marker for Proportional Bandwidth Allocation
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we study why the traditional traffic markers cannot provide precision of marking and proportional fairness in the current differentiated service (DiffServ) networks. To solve these problems, we propose the innovation three color marker (ITCM) algorithm. Our proposed ITCM algorithm calculates both the long term average rate and the instantaneous rate of traffic when marking the packet. Moreover, our proposed algorithm achieves the proportional fair sharing among aggregates by marking the packet as yellow with probability in proportion to CIR. We have compared the performance of our proposed ITCM marker with traditional markers. Simulation results show that our proposed algorithm performs better than traditional markers in the case of under-subscription. It is not only achieves the target rate, but also achieves proportional fairness of sharing the excess bandwidth

articleTitle: Pre-Settable Adiabatic Flip-Flops and Sequential Circuits
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, the design of pre-settable adiabatic flip-flops and sequential circuits based on the two-phase CPAL (complementary pass-transistor adiabatic logic) is presented. The two-phase CPAL is more suitable for the design of flip-flops and sequential circuits, as it uses fewer transistors than the conventional CMOS implementation and the other adiabatic logic circuits. Pre-settable adiabatic flip-flops (D and T) based on the two-phase CPAL are proposed. Adiabatic flip-flops with a reset line are more universal and suitable for the design of sequential circuits. A practical sequential system realized with the proposed pre-adiabatic flip-flops is demonstrated. SPICE simulations show that the energy loss of the proposed pre-settable adiabatic flip-flop and sequential circuits is greatly reduced compared to the conventional CMOS implementation

articleTitle: A Self-Adjusted Genetic Algorithm Applied to VOD Cluster
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In order to improve the throughput, response speed and scalability of VOD server efficiently, many VOD server have thrown away single servers and turn into VOD server clusters, which centrally accepts all the coming requests and evenly dispatches them to the servers in the cluster. Weighted Round-Robin, weighted least connections algorithms which commonly used in VOD cluster show low efficiencies, because they either do not consider the difference in performance between servers or do not consider the contents of coming different requests. In this paper analyzes and explores the load balancing technology of VOD cluster server, and puts forward a self-adjusted genetic algorithm. The experimental results are perfect

articleTitle: An Hybrid Evaluative Algorithm Applied to Task Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Since the task scheduling in grid computing faces a NP-hard problem, it leads very difficult to validate the methods of task scheduling. This paper combined with the advantages of two evaluative algorithms: genetic algorithm and simulated annealing, brings forward an hybrid evaluative algorithm and applied to solve task scheduling problem in grid computing. From the analysis and experiment result, it is concluded that this algorithm is superior to genetic algorithm and simulated annealing

articleTitle: An Improved All Digital Timing Tracking Loop in OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: When all digital phase-locked loop (PLL) is applied in OFDM systems, there are two important problems that must be solved, namely how to normalize the error signal and how to avoid the phenomenon of out-of-lock in multipath fading channel. This paper has studied the two problems and put forward a suitable solution scheme. The studying results show that the proposed scheme can really effectively solve the problem of timing tracking for OFDM systems and make PLL work normally in multipath fading channels.

articleTitle: Traffic Lifetime-Aware Routing Based on Grooming Policy in a WDM Network
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Routing and grooming have often been studied independently for WDM networks. However, a closer investigation shows that they are indeed closely related, and better performance can be obtained by integrating them. In this paper, we propose an integrated scheme for routing and grooming in a WDM network. In this scheme, routing decision is made combined with the grooming policy. In addition, traffic lifetime is taken into account in routing and grooming. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can improve resource utilization on existing lightpaths and leave more free resource for future requests. As a result, wavelength can be used more efficiently and lower blocking probability is achieved

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband and Low-Power Amplifier Using 0.35-μm SiGe BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: We propose a unique wideband amplifier configuration. The new configuration adopts an improved Darlington amplifier to broaden the bandwidth and flatten the output gain. The low power consumption and matched impedances are also achieved in our amplifier. This circuit has been realized using Toshiba 0.35 mum SiGe BiCMOS technology with the fT of 30 GHz. The simulation result of the presented amplifier demonstrates 1-10 GHz bandwidth and 11.3-dB maximum forward gain (S21) with less than plusmn0.5-dB gain flatness while it drains 8 mA from a 3-V supply. A 1-dB compression point and an IIP3 of -12.5 dBm and 6 dBm respectively also have been reported in this paper.

articleTitle: Capacity and Coverage Analyses for the Generalized Distributed Cellular Architecture-Group Cell
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper provides a novel cellular structure: generalized distributed cellular architecture-group cell, which is suitable for advanced physical techniques and solves the problem of smaller cells caused by higher carrier frequency used in future. The concept and the structure of the group cell are described and the slide handover strategy based on the group cell is introduced in details. The system capacity analyses with Shannon analyses and coverage analyses based on outage probability are presented in theory analysis. Finally, compared to traditional cellular structure, the simulation results show the capacity and coverage merits brought by group cell architecture

articleTitle: Nonparametric Complex Background Prediction Algorithm Using FCM Clustering for Dim Point Infrared Targets Detection
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A nonparametric background prediction algorithm using fuzzy c-means (FCM) clustering is proposed to enhance the detection of dim small infrared targets in image data. The target of interest is assumed to have a very small spatial spread, and is obscured by heavy background clutter. The input image data is firstly segmented using FCM clustering, and then the nonparametric regressive method is applied to predict background in each cluster respectively. Subsequently the background is subtracted from the input data, leaving components of the target signal in the residual noise. Experiment results show better detecting performance for the output data by the algorithm of this paper than by other traditional methods

articleTitle: Real-Time Tracking of Athletes in Diving Training Videos
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a system for real-time tracking of athletes in diving training scenes. The system employs a cascade framework, and only certain regions of interest (ROI) where the athletes could appear are processed. First, background subtraction method is performed in current ROI to extract foreground regions; then, non-human foreground objects such as the springboards are excluded using prior information; next the ROI is modified so that in next frame the athlete would still be in it; finally, a fast curve-fitting algorithm is proposed to get the contour of the athlete. The curve-fitting algorithm is not sensitive to initial curve position and is able to overcome small gaps, which exist commonly in the foreground regions. The system runs at 25 HZ for 720 x 576 color images on a P4 3.0 GHZ PC

articleTitle: A Robust Digit Recognition Model Research with Low Signal Noise Ratio
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this article, we absorbed the basic idea of DP in normalizing the temporal evolving characteristics of speech observation vector sequences, and designed a low SNR English digit recognition model based on whole MFCC sequences. Such model not only carries effectively the whole information but also normalizes the digit feature sequences by adjusting dynamically the frame length of each spoken digit, which can adapt the different speaking rates. By using frame time filter and Multi Sub-Spectrum filter, noise interference to the digit can be partly reduced and the model's adaptability to the backgrounds be improved. The experiment shows that the English digit error rate has reduced 30% at least, and 68.71% for best result after adding the new processing modules. In addition, the model is simple in structure and low in computation, and also easy to realize real time processing.

articleTitle: Joint Spatial-Frequency Opportunistic Multiuser Diversity for VBLAST OFDMA
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: For OFDMA system, the greedy subcarrier and bit loading can be adopted to exploit the multiuser diversity in frequency domain for the independent fading of different users and achive higher cell throughput without considering the user fairness. Meanwhile in MIMO scenario, different UE experience independent spatial fading for different location, and thus the different antenna at the Base Station (BS) can be allocated to diffferent UEs to exploit the spatial multiuser diversity gain. In this paper, the Joint Spatial-Frequency Opportunistic Multiuser scheduling is proposed for VBLAST OFDMA downlink to obtain the spatial-frequency multiuser diversity and better throughput performance. As only partial CSI is available at the transmitter, the SNR of the post-detection of every transmit antennas are feedback, the total power of BS is divided into every antenna of every subcarrier uniformly. The simulaton results shows that the proposed algorithm is better than that of frequency domain greedy algorithm by 20%.

articleTitle: On Queue Length of RPR
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Resilient packet ring (RPR) is a new technology has just been standardized as IEEE 802.17 for metropolitan area networks (MAN). RPR can be regarded as a buffer (or register) insertion ring. Thus, the buffer size configuration is very important to the performance of RPR. Currently, it is lacked for its theoretic analysis. In this paper, we initiated RPR's queue length into queuing theory and investigated their relations with throughput and number of nodes. The results are very close to those of engineering. It also turns out some new points such as queue length does not increase linearly with number of nodes as in our imagination

articleTitle: Use Augmented Connection Boxes to Improve FPGA Performance
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: With the rapid progress of VLSI technology FPGAs' performance efficiency has become the main concern of designers and manufacturers. Our goal in this work is to propose a new FPGA structure to reduce critical net delay without increasing routing area. The augmented connection box is proposed. It allows two different signals to share one track in a connection box by inserting additional switches where logic pins have connection with tracks. The experimental results prove that the augmented connection box improves FPGAs' delay performance by avoiding detour when nets are routed and the possible delay increase incurred by switch addition does not happen. Also channel width is reduced a lot

articleTitle: A VHF OTA-C Topology Having Low Phase Error With Gm Tuning
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In sub-micron process, while speed of device is suitable for VHF applications, phase variation at unity gain frequency of OTA-C cell with frequency tuning is high. This is mainly because of high value of channel length modulation parameter of the devices. A technique which makes the phase response robust to frequency tuning is proposed here. Based on this technique a VHF CMOS OTA-C cell is designed in a 0.18 mum CMOS process. The phase error of the cell is within 0.3deg, over a range of unity-gain frequency from 300 MHz to 1.2 GHz. The small phase error over a wide range of frequency implies the use of just one Q-tuning loop for all the integrators having unity-gain frequency within this range. Also this makes this circuit suitable for application in programmable transfer function filters

articleTitle: Genetic Network Programming for Artificial Stock Market
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Combined with the idea of Austrian school of economics, this paper proposes a new multi-agent model for artificial stock market based on genetic network programming. It focuses on applying the GNP approach to emulate investment behavior of agents and evolve their trading rules. Simultaneously, this model enhances the heterogeneity of agents, and searches for an optimal combination of parameter values based on GA. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of this GNP-ASM model through comparison with empirical statistics

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Compressing Optical Pulse by Using Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Compression of optical pulse in a mode-locked fiber laser constructed from photonic crystal fibers (PCFs) is investigated experimentally. In the experiment, photonic crystal fiber is used as an intracavity compression media. The high nonlinearity and anomalous dispersion of the photonic crystal fiber can cause intracavity compression resulting in a significant reduction in the pulse width. The pulses duration at the repletion rate of 10 GHz was less than 10 ps over a range of 1532-1565 nm

articleTitle: An Efficient Method to Determine the Weight Distributions of Binary Quadratic Residue Codes
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Recently, a fast algorithm for determining the weight distributions of half-rate linear codes was introduced by Gaborit et al. In this paper, we propose an efficient method to determine the weight distributions of binary extended quadratic residue codes. Compared with the method developed by Gaborit et al., the proposed method gains slightly improvements in the computation. Also, the weight distributions of the binary (152, 76, 20) extended quadratic residue code are given

articleTitle: A Novel Dynamic Current Analysis for ADC Testing
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The increasing importance of mixed-signal circuits has brought about a new important issue in testing this kind of circuits. Nevertheless, these techniques are difficult and costly. In an attempt to promote mixed-signal circuits testing, a novel fault detection method is presented in this paper. This method uses wavelet transform based dynamic current (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dd</sub>) analysis to detect the faults. The experimental results for an ADC circuit show that the proposed method not only can effectively detect faults, but also have higher sensitivity than integral and FFT method. Furthermore, the impact of different mother wavelet on the sensitivity of fault detection is addressed

articleTitle: Study on the Cage Net Crack Detection Facility of Sea Cage
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: To the problems on the cage net crack detectability, a new cage net crack detecting method and detecting system is designed. This facility, comprised of single-chip microcomputer, cage net crack detecting circuit, switch matrix and cellular phone mold piece, could detect the situation of cage net crack in muddy water area with lower power consume and low cost. The net slice could become a cage net crack sensor by weaving lead and nylon into it. The system divides cage net into many net slices, and codes each one. As soon as one of the net slices is cracked, the loop between the damaged position, sea water, and the sea electrode are formed and then let the system send short message to users by cellphone module, included the cracked sea cage's serial number and the information of crack part. When the conjunction breakdown between the system and the net slices occurs, it could let the system send short message to users, including the sea cage's serial number and the information of break part. Compared to traditional methods, this detection system is novel, so awarded two national invention patents.

articleTitle: Funcational Test with Single Compaction Output for Digital IP Cores
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a novel functional test methodology with single compaction output for embedded digital intellectual property cores on a system-on-a-chip is proposed. The functional test method is independent of the fault model and the structure of the core under test and uses only the knowledge of the test set and corresponding fault-free responses. In addition, advantages of our approach include single compaction output and implementation only by single test application. Hence, as test time consumption is concerned, the method excels those counterparts, in which single compaction output with zero-aliasing is obtained via two step or two mode. Also, in order to lower hardware overhead, encoding technique is adopted to both normal response and practical response during test application, so we improved the idea to deal with similar problem

articleTitle: A Novel Frequency Offset Estimator for OFDM
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The frequency offset estimation for OFDM systems using the correlations of several identical parts in the preamble is addressed. We design a novel preamble which is composed of one irregular OFDM training symbol block with odd numbers of identical parts and one regular OFDM training symbol block with even numbers of identical parts. Based on the designed preamble, we propose a novel frequency offset estimator. Simulation results show that the proposed frequency offset estimator has the larger estimate range advantage over the conventional estimator while maintaining approximately the same performance

articleTitle: A LDPC-Based Joint Source Channel Decoding Using HMM for Image Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A modified joint source channel decoding (JSCD) algorithm based on low-density parity-check (LDPC) coding and hidden Markov estimation is proposed to employ the self-checking mechanism of LDPC codes in adjusting the error probability p of the hidden Markov model (HMM) and the JSCD scheme utilizes the source residual redundancy while no priori information of the source parameters is available. We also extend and apply the algorithm over image transmission system. Simulation results show that the modified JSCD algorithm leads to the joint decoder converge at least 10% faster than the unmodified method without any degradation in the decoding performance. The method also obtains substantial improved performance in image quality of 3.0 dB-8.0 dB (PSNR) at 0.6 dB in E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> when it is employed in still image transmission systems

articleTitle: Faster and More Stabile-Asymmetric Bidirectional Weighting Topologies on PSO
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new algorithm, called the asymmetric fully informed particle swarm optimization (AFIPSO), is proposed. It mends the FIPSO algorithm by newly constructing weighting functions, which realizes asymmetric influence between two particles. Then six weighting functions and their four cross combinations are tested. The simulation results have shown that the performance of the algorithm with the compounding-form of weighting functions is far better than the primary version, faster and more stabile in convergence, especially with perfect convergent rate

articleTitle: An OFDM Impulse Canceller with Impulse Detection
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Generally, OFDM has immunity to the impulse noise. However, the performance of OFDM system will degrade seriously if the power of the impulse noise is above a certain threshold. In this paper, an impulse noise canceller based on the Reed-Solomon decoding with impulse detection will be proposed. As the uniform spaced pilots in frequency domain are employed as the syndromes, and the space between the pilots is coprime with the number of the subcarriers, such an assignment of the pilots will possess an innate interleaving property. The recursive extension is proposed to reconstruct the impulsive noise in frequency domain. And it can reduce the implementation complexity. The effectiveness of the algorithms is verified by simulations

articleTitle: Stabilize Unstable Equilibrium Points for A New Class of Simple 3-Neuron Chaotic Cellular Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The unstable equilibrium points of a new class of simple 3-neuron chaotic cellular neural network can be stabilized very easily via linear feedback control. The stability condition is obtained. Simulations results indicate that this method in the paper is available

articleTitle: The Optimal Transmission Strategy for MIMO Wireless Systems with Covariance Feedback
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The optimal transmission strategy in terms of outage probability for spatially correlated multi-input multi-output (MIMO) system is studied in this paper. With covariance feedback the receiver is assumed to have perfect channel state information (CSI) while the transmitter knows only the transmit correlation matrix and receive correlation matrix. The optimal transmit directions turn out to be orthogonal directions along the eigenvectors of the transmit correlation matrix and independent of the receive correlation matrix. While the optimal power allocation scheme is related to both transmit and receive correlation matrices. Numerical results show the advantage of optimal power allocation strategy over equal power allocation and beamforming schemes

articleTitle: A CMOS Front-end Circuit for SONET OC-96 Receiver
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: An optical receiver front-end for SONET OC-96 receivers was analyzed and designed in 0.18 mum CMOS process. It consists of a transimpedance amplifier (TIA) and a limiting amplifier (LA). The TIA takes a fully differential configuration, and regulated cascode (RGC) input stage is implemented. The LA was realized by five cascaded identical gain stages with active inductor load. The TIA achieved 4.2 GHz bandwidth for 0.5 pF photodiode (PD) capacitance and 1.2 kOmega transimpedance gain. The LA achieved 5.4 GHz bandwidth and 29 dB voltage gain. The optical sensitivity is -19 dBm at 5-Gb/s for a bit-error rate of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup>, and it dissipates 45.5 mW for 1.8 V supply

articleTitle: Design and the Application of Large-Scale Matrix and Complex Control Network
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In the process of city modernization, higher and higher requirements are raised to the control of environment lighting landscape and building device. They have common features such as multi-points, large scale, realtime control and exact synchronization demands of dynamic control. This paper proposes sequence synchronization and extract synchronization and presents the integrated system design of a large-scale matrix control network, including its main procedure, the area and field controllers, remote control interface, and its correlative computation as well. Its application proves that Ethernet-CAN large-scale matrix control complex network has a broad prospect.

articleTitle: Fusion of Curve Target Based on Sparse Sampling
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: An effective method to fuse open curve target is present. The indexes and rules for fusion are founded on open curve moments, a new type of moments reformulated on close curve moments. Experimental results show the fusion rules work well

articleTitle: A New Forward-Secure Signcryption Scheme
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Signcryption scheme combines digital signature and encryption functions. In regular signcryption, once the long-term private key is compromised, all signatures even those were issued by the honest signer before the compromise, will not be trustworthy any more. In the paper, we present a new forward-secure signcryption scheme. The forward security is that this key update function is one-way and, given the secret key for the current period, it is hard to compute any of the previously used secret keys. So even the adversary gets the secret key, it is still hard to compute any of the previously used secret keys. In this paper, we combine signcryption and forward-secure to present a new signcryption scheme with forward secrecy

articleTitle: A Type-II Hybrid ARQ Scheme Based on Rate-compatible LDPC Code
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Rate-compatible code is a typical way to achieve high forward error correction (ARQ/FEC) systems in packet data transmission. This paper focuses on the construction of efficient rate-compatible low density parity check (RC-LDPC) codes in a flexible way. A special technique to get rate compatible LDPC codes called extending without code-rate threshold is presented in comparison to the results in Zhu Miao et al. (2005), with code-rate threshold. Based on the improved scheme, a type-II hybrid ARQ scheme is presented in the paper, which is greatly flexible and results in good performance. The throughput performances of different full incremental redundancy (FIR) schemes depend on the length of retransmitted incremental redundancy (IR) substantially. Furthermore, performance comparison between full incremental redundancy (FIR) based on this rate-compatible structure and chase combing (CC) protocols has been investigated

articleTitle: The Rules Reduction of Web Information Filtering
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The Web information filtering is the research hotspot of network information security technique. This paper puts forward an approach of the rules reduction based on the rough set in Web information filtering. By using attribute reduction and value reduction, we can get the optimizing filter rules. Furthermore, this approach will improve the handling speed and practicability of information filtering analysis. The specimens show that this method is available

articleTitle: Wavelet Scale and Wavelength in Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The relationship between scale and wavelength in wavelet transform is investigated. First, the definition of wavelet transform with scale-energy parameter is given, its corresponding properties in time (spatial)-frequency domain are presented. Then, the method is proposed to how to get the relationship between scale and wavelength; the relationship formulas for several commonly used wavelets are given. Finally, an illustrative example of the relationship between scale and wavelength in Morlet wavelet is presented and simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed formulas

articleTitle: PVPSU: Publicly Verifiable and Parallel Share Updates for Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Based on RSA algorithm, this paper provides a publicly verifiable and parallel share update algorithm for mobile ad hoc networks. According to Diffie-Hellman assumption and public verifiability, this new algorithm improves security and robustness. In addition, communication rounds have been decreased from three to two. This paper also proposes a new multiplicative shuffle scheme for share updates. Our simulation and implementation evaluate and confirm that the solution is effective

articleTitle: A 15-bit 10-Msample/s Pipelined A/D Converter Based on Incomplete Settling Principle
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a 15-bit 10-MS/s pipelined ADC. To implement the incomplete settling principle, the traditional complete settling stage is improved to the incomplete settling structure through dividing the sampling clock of the traditional stage into two parts for discharging the sampling and feedback capacitors and completing the sampling, respectively. It verifies the correction and validity of optimizing ADCs' conversion speed without increasing power consumption through the incomplete settling. It is processed in 0.18 mum 1P6M CMOS mixed-mode technology. Simulation results show that 82 dB SNDR and 87 dB SFDR are obtained at the sampling rate of 10 MHz with the input sine frequency of 100 KHz and the whole static power dissipation is 21.94 mW

articleTitle: A Novel TR-STBC-OFDM Scheme for MIMO-OFDM
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper combines time-reversal space-time block coding (TR-STBC) which is for frequency-selective channel, with orthogonal frequency multiplexing (OFDM) to derive a new MIMO-OFDM system. Compared with the system which adopts STBC proposed by Alamouti, this one adopting TR-STBC exchanges the positions of OFDM modulator/demodulator and Space-time coder/decoder to reduce the computation complexity. Through simulation results, it can be seen that this scheme has better performance and can also achieve full diversity gain

articleTitle: Integration of NCW Sensor Networks and the Grid
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Sensor networks consist of large numbers of network sensors that can be dynamically deployed in the battlefield and used for situational awareness in network centric warfare (NCW). In this paper, our purpose is to dynamically integrate these sensor networks with grid service to support real-time sensing, exploitation and decision-making in a rich tactical environment. Heterogeneous sensors' capabilities are described with XML so that grid service can be dynamically discovered and used by various end-user and intermediate processing applications. In addition, we simulate our middleware model with the help of GT3.

articleTitle: A New Fractional NPLL Device for High Precision Spectrum Analysis
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper describes the theory of non-uniform sampling realization about DFT first, then propose a new fractional NPLL (F-NPLL) device for approximating the ideal synchronous sampling. The new device can reduce the maximal time wrap within 0.5 T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mu</sub> and reduce spectrum leakage of DFT effectively

articleTitle: A 10 GHz VCO in SiGe BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a 10 GHz VCO (voltage controlled oscillator) based on 0.35 um SiGe BiCMOS technology is presented. It is designed for 10 Gb/s CRC (clock recovery circuit) in optical communication systems and X band wireless applications. Cross coupled differential topology is adopted. It can operate from 9.78 GHz to 10.35 GHz with a phase noise of -106 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset. For the 1.8 V supply voltage, the total power consumption is 12 mW. And the chip area is only 0.17 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Novel Turbo Equalization for MIMO Frequency Selective Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel CRC-aided turbo equalization approach that exploits the cyclic redundancy check (CRC) to reduce computational complexity. The essential idea is that, during the iterative process, once a data block in the data frame is detected totally correct by CRC, we can set all the log likelihood ratio (LLR) of the bits in this block a fixed high value for the next iteration, and stop the corresponding computation about this block, hence decreasing computation in equalization and decoding. When LDPC is used as forward-error correction (FEC) codes, it is convenient to make use of the error detection capability of LDPC instead of CRC, avoiding extra overhead. Simulations show that the proposed CRC-aided turbo equalization achieves a performance equal to or even better than that of the conventional turbo equalization algorithm, but with a lower computational complexity

articleTitle: Enhanced Low-Density Parity-Check Codes Based on Sum-check Blocks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Based on some characteristics of decoding and error-floors of low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes, an approach of adding sum-check blocks to original LDPC blocks over GF(2) is proposed. The performance of this approach is analyzed and the circuits are also presented. Also, the simulation results show that the performance of the constructed LDPC codes can be improved significantly with low cost, as the block error probability (BEP) drops

articleTitle: Performance of Variable Rate and Variable Power MQAM System Based on Bit Error Rate and Channel Estimates
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: We consider the effect of an imperfect channel estimate on a variable rate and variable power (VRVP) multilevel quadrature amplitude modulation (MQAM) system, where the transmit power and data rate are varied relative to the estimate of the received signal. Based on the VRVP-MQAM system operating over a Rayleigh flat-fading channel, we derive a bit error rate (BER) estimator using a maximum aposteriori (MAP) estimation approach. We apply the BER estimator to the VRVP-MQAM system, and thereby derive and obtain system expressions which are applicable to any channel estimation technique. In addition, the resulting formulations are also useful for analyzing the effect of channel state information (CSI). Consequently, we derive and obtain an optimal solution for our proposed system and generate numerical results to compare the variations of system performance with imperfect CSI

articleTitle: Design of the Program-controlled Complex Permittivity Testing System with Quasi-Optical Resonator at Millimeter-wave Band
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper introduces the design of a program- controlled system used for complex permittivity measurement in millimeter-wave band via quasi-optical resonator. The program-controlled system consists of several functional modules, such as testing module, data processing module, etc., fulfills automatic testing of the complex permittivity and tangent of the loss angle. Being programmed in OOP (Object-Oriented Programming) language and adopting user interface with Windows style, the system is friendly to users and easy to operate.

articleTitle: Outage Probability Analysis of the Dual-Branch Transmit-Selective System over Correlated Modified Weibull Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this work, first, we deduce the probability density function (PDF) and the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the fading coefficient envelope, based on the correlated modified Weibull fading model. To simply the discussion, a system with two transmit antennas and one receive antenna is considered, namely dual-branch system. Secondly, the outage probability of the dual-branch system under the correlated modified Weibull fading channel is derived. And the effects of the correlation coefficient and the Weibull fading parameter on the performance are analyzed by computer simulation for QPSK modulation. Finally, we present several simulations to validate our analysis. Results show that the simulation curves fit our analytical results correctly

articleTitle: Joint Estimation of Cyclic Frequency and Direction of Arrival Based on Cyclic-Frequency-Beamspace
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new method for estimation of cyclic frequency and direction of arrival (DOA) is presented. A cyclic-frequency-beamspace data model is established, and then is used to estimate cyclic frequency and DOA by using Pro-ESPRIT, beamspace-ESPRIT and an integer search algorithm. Numerical simulation results illustrate the availability of the proposed method

articleTitle: Constructing and Application of Adaptive Spline Wavelet Filter Coefficients in Image Edge Detection
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The selection of wavelet scale and filter coefficients is a key technology for wavelet edge detection. In this paper, we propose an algorithm of constructing adaptive spline wavelet filter coefficients based on the genetic algorithm. We detect image edges by employing the obtained filter coefficients, and obtain a good effect of edge extraction by integrating the edge connection algorithm. Finally, experimental results are compared with Canny's operator, and demonstrate the performance of our algorithm

articleTitle: A Novel Robust Cyclostationary Beamformer Based On Conjugate Gradient Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Based on conjugate gradient (CG) algorithm, the authors propose a novel robust cyclostationary beamformer algorithm, which can be used to extract signals with cyclostationarity in the presence of cycle frequency error (CFE). Compared to conventional cyclostationary beamforming algorithm, the proposed approach doesn't need to estimate the actual cycle frequency, and can get higher output signal-to- interference plus noise ratio (SINR)

articleTitle: Design, Implementation and Testing of the Controller for the Terabit Packet Switch
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The sequential greedy scheduling (SGS) is a scalable algorithm that provides non-blocking in high-capacity packet switches. We implemented the SGS scheduler in the FPGA device, and examined its scalability and speed. Then, we developed the software for design testing. Our testing software confirms the correct functioning of the scheduler. Both, the scheduler implementation, and the testing software are presented in this paper

articleTitle: NarrowBand Interference Mitigation for Space-Frequency Trellis Coded MIMO-OFDM
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Coded OFDM (orthogonal frequency diversion multiplexing) with a MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) configuration is a popular method for high data wireless transmission. SFTC (space-frequency trellis codes) coded MIMO-OFDM makes the system more robust to the various types of interference. In this paper, MIMO-OFDM with SFTC in narrowband interference (NBI) environment is considered. It is shown that a simple antenna selection scheme can be proposed to NBI mitigation, at high signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR). The effect of the NBI and the performance improvement of the scheme is also examined through analysis and simulations

articleTitle: Non-stationary and Small-time Scaling Behavior of Internet Traffic
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Scaling behaviors of traffic influence network modeling, service providing and traffic engineering. So it has been the focus of many researches.
